then: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about the Sur and said {idea}it is a horn that will be blown{/idea}. He said the one holding it is waiting for permission. When the Companions asked what to say, he told them: {reward}Allah is sufficient for us, and the best Protector; upon Allah we rely{/reward}.
now: You read about the end of the world and your chest tightens. The Companions felt that too. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ did not tell them to panic.{/idea} He gave them a sentence of trust to hold.
old: Thinking about the Last Day should just make me scared.
new: The Prophet ﷺ answered that fear with trust: Allah is enough for us.
try: Say "HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal wakeel" three times today, slowly.

title: Whispering: we only stayed about ten days.
subtitle: How short life will feel
then: Ibn Abbas said they will be {idea}whispering among themselves{/idea}. They will say they stayed in the world only about ten days. The whole of life, looked back on, will seem like {trap}a little while{/trap}.
now: You keep saying "one day" I will start praying properly, fix things with my father, give more. {idea}Your whole life may feel like ten days when it is over.{/idea} "One day" is shorter than you think.
old: I have plenty of time to get serious later.
new: Life will feel like a few days when it ends. The time to act is now.
try: Do one thing today you have been postponing to "one day".

title: The wisest among them will say: only a single day.
subtitle: The clearest mind sees it even shorter
then: Ibn Kathir explains the one with the best mind will say {idea}one day{/idea}, because life's repeating nights, days and hours will feel like a single day. He cites another verse: {trap}you stayed but a little, if you had only known{/trap}.
now: Ask your grandmother how fast her life went. She will say, "Like a blink." {idea}The wiser you get, the shorter life looks.{/idea} So spend today like it matters, because it is a big piece of the whole.
old: Life is long, and today is just one of many.
new: The wisest see life as one day. Today is a big share of it.
try: Ask an elder today how fast life felt to them, and listen.

title: The mountains? My Lord will blow them away.
subtitle: Even the most solid things are temporary

row.title: only Allah
sub: and what is done for Him

then: People asked {idea}whether the mountains would remain on the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. The answer: My Lord will {trap}take them from their places, wipe them out and remove them completely{/trap}, scattered like dust.
now: The house you are paying off for 25 years. The company that has been around a century. The body you work so hard on at the gym. {idea}If mountains go, so will these.{/idea}
old: Some things in my life are solid and will always be there.
new: Even mountains will be blown away. Only what I do for Allah lasts.
try: Look at something that feels permanent today and say: this too will pass, Allah remains.

title: The whole earth left a flat, open plain.
subtitle: Nowhere left to hide
then: Ibn Kathir explains the earth becomes {idea}one expanse spread out{/idea}, level land. Some said it also means bare, with nothing growing. With the mountains gone, {trap}nothing is left standing between people and what is coming{/trap}.
now: You keep a few things hidden: the browser history, the side conversations, the version of you at work. {idea}One day the ground will be flat and open.{/idea} Living now as if nothing is hidden is a kind of freedom.
old: Some parts of my life can stay out of view forever.
new: One day everything will be in the open. I can start living openly now.
try: Clear out one hidden thing today that you would not want seen on that open plain.

title: Not a dip, not a rise anywhere.
subtitle: Every rank and level flattened
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others said there will be {idea}no valley, no hill, no place low or high{/idea}. The earth that once had peaks and pits becomes completely even.
now: At work there is the corner office and the cleaner's cupboard. On the street, the big car and the bus stop. {idea}On that plain, nobody stands higher.{/idea} Treat people today the way they will be seen then.
old: Some people are simply above others.
new: One day the ground will be level. Only what I did will lift me.
try: Greet one person today you usually walk past, like the cleaner or the security guard.

title: Everyone follows the Caller, and voices fall silent.
subtitle: Obedience that comes too late
then: On that Day people will {idea}rush to the Caller wherever they are commanded{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes: {trap}if they had been like this in the worldly life, it would have helped them{/trap}, but there it does not. Ibn Abbas said nothing is heard but the steps of feet.
now: The adhan goes off on your phone and you hit snooze. One day you will run toward a call without hesitation. {idea}Answering now is what counts.{/idea}
old: I will respond to Allah's call when I am ready.
new: Everyone will answer that final call. Answering His call today is what helps me.
try: Respond to the very next adhan you hear within five minutes.

title: Intercession helps only by the Most Merciful's permission.
subtitle: No one speaks without His leave
then: Ibn Kathir explains no intercession helps {idea}except by Allah's permission{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ described falling in prostration under the Throne until told: {reward}intercede, and your intercession will be accepted{/reward}. Allah will bring out whoever has even a speck of faith.
now: You think, "My family is religious, my father was an imam, I will be fine." {idea}No one speaks for you without Allah's leave.{/idea} But His mercy reaches even a tiny seed of faith, so guard yours.
old: Being connected to good people will get me through.
new: All help on that Day comes by His permission. My own faith, however small, matters.
try: Ask Allah today to make you among those the Prophet ﷺ intercedes for.

title: He knows what is ahead and behind them.
subtitle: His knowledge surrounds ours
then: Ibn Kathir explains {idea}He encompasses all creation with His knowledge{/idea}, what has happened to them and what will happen. And people {trap}never encompass anything of His knowledge{/trap} except what He wills.
now: You lie awake trying to plan every outcome: the job, the move, the kids' future. {idea}You cannot see the whole.{/idea} He already knows what is ahead of you, and what is behind you that you have forgotten.
old: If I think hard enough, I can see how everything will turn out.
new: Only Allah sees what is before and behind me. I can plan and then trust.
try: Write down one worry about the future, then say: Allah knows what I do not.

title: All faces humbled; whoever carries wrongdoing fails.
subtitle: Before the Ever-Living, every wrong is settled
then: Ibn Abbas said all creatures will be {idea}humbled before the Ever-Living who does not die, the Sustainer who does not sleep{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says Allah will give every right to its owner, even {trap}the hornless ram against the horned one{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said wrongdoing will be darkness on that Day.
now: The money you borrowed and never returned. The sharp word to your younger brother. The colleague whose credit you took. {idea}Every wrong gets settled.{/idea} Settle it now, while it is easy.
old: Small wrongs I did long ago do not matter anymore.
new: Every wrong will be settled. Better to put it right while I still can.
try: Return one thing or apologise for one wrong today, however small.

title: Do good with faith, and fear no unfairness.
subtitle: Nothing added, nothing taken away
then: After the warning comes the comfort. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said the believer who does good {reward}will not have his evils increased or his good deeds decreased{/reward}. Ibn Kathir explains Zulm is others' sins added to you; Hadm is your good being reduced. {idea}Neither will happen.{/idea}
now: You do your best at work and someone else gets the credit. You help family and nobody notices. Life is not always fair. {reward}Allah's judgement is.{/reward} Not one good deed will be shaved off.
old: My good deeds might get lost or not counted.
new: With faith, every good I do is fully kept. Nothing unfair will touch me.
try: Do one good deed today that you know no one will ever thank you for.

title: Warnings repeated in many ways, so they might wake up.
subtitle: Why the Quran says it more than once

row.title: care
sub: one of them will reach me

then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran came {idea}as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, in clear Arabic{/idea}. The warnings are varied so people will {reward}leave off sins{/reward}, or so it will {reward}produce acts of obedience that bring them closer to Allah{/reward}.
now: Your mother reminds you for the fifth time to call your grandmother. It feels like nagging. Then one day it lands. {idea}Repetition is how love gets through.{/idea} The Quran repeats for the same reason.
old: I have heard this warning before, so I can skip it.
new: Allah repeats it in different ways because one of them might finally reach me.
try: Next time you read a familiar warning verse, ask: what is it saying to me today?

title: Do not rush; say: my Lord, increase me in knowledge.
subtitle: Listening fully, then asking for more
then: Ibn Abbas said the Prophet ﷺ {trap}went through great pains to retain the revelation{/trap}, moving his tongue quickly with Jibril. Allah made it easier: listen quietly, and We will gather it in your chest. Ibn Uyaynah said {reward}the Prophet ﷺ kept increasing in knowledge until Allah took him{/reward}.
now: You start a course, a hifz plan, a new skill, and try to cram it all in one week. Then you burn out. {idea}Listen, take it in, and keep asking for more.{/idea} Knowledge grows over a lifetime.
old: I need to learn everything quickly or I will lose it.
new: I can learn calmly, trust Allah to keep it in me, and keep asking for more.
try: Say "Rabbi zidni ilma" before you study or read anything today.

title: Adam was given a promise, and he forgot.
subtitle: Forgetting is in the human name
then: Ibn Abbas said {idea}man was named Insan because he was given a covenant, but he forgot it{/idea}. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said "forgot" means he abandoned it. Allah found in him {trap}no firm willpower{/trap}. The story of Adam begins with a very human weakness.
now: You set a goal on 1 January and by February it is gone. You promise yourself no more late-night scrolling, and there you are at 1am. {idea}Forgetting is part of being human{/idea}. The point is what you do when you remember.
old: I keep forgetting my promises, so I must be a bad person.
new: Forgetting is human, starting with Adam. Turning back when I remember is what matters.
try: Write down one promise to Allah you forgot, and renew it today with one small step.

title: The angels bowed to Adam, but Iblis refused.
subtitle: Where the enmity began
then: Ibn Kathir says this shows {reward}how Adam was honored{/reward} and favored over much of creation. The angels prostrated as a sign of honor. {trap}Iblis refused and became arrogant{/trap}. From here began his enmity for Adam and his children.
now: A younger colleague gets promoted over you, and something inside refuses to congratulate them. {trap}That refusal to bow to what Allah decided{/trap} is the oldest sin there is. Notice it when it rises.
old: I have good reasons for not accepting someone else's honor.
new: Refusing what Allah gave someone else is the arrogance of Iblis. I can choose to bow.
try: Congratulate one person today on something you secretly envied them for.

title: This is your enemy: do not let him drive you out.
subtitle: A clear warning, given in advance

row.title: Iblis
sub: enemy to you and your wife

then: Allah told Adam: {trap}this is an enemy to you and your wife{/trap}, Hawwa. Ibn Kathir explains: do not be hasty in doing something that gets you expelled, or {trap}you will be tired, uncomfortable and worried, seeking your living{/trap}. In Paradise there was ease.
now: You know the exact trigger: the late night, the certain app, the particular friend. {idea}The enemy has been named for you already.{/idea} Knowing his face is half the protection.
old: Temptation catches me completely by surprise.
new: Allah already named my enemy. I can learn his tricks and stay alert.
try: Write down your top trigger for doing wrong, and one plan to avoid it this week.

title: Here you will never be hungry or unclothed.
subtitle: Inner and outer need, both covered
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah {idea}combined hunger and nakedness{/idea} because hunger is an inner humiliation and nakedness an outer one. Adam was told {reward}both were taken care of{/reward}. He lacked nothing, inside or out.
now: Your fridge has food. Your wardrobe has clothes. Yet you scroll the sales page feeling like something is missing. {idea}Notice what is already covered{/idea}, before the whisper of "more" arrives.
old: I will be content once I get the next thing.
new: Much of what I need is already given. Seeing that makes me harder to trick.
try: Before buying anything non-essential today, name three things you already have.

title: No thirst there, and no burning sun.
subtitle: The other half of the promise
then: Ibn Kathir notes these two are also a pair: {idea}thirst is an inner heat, the sun's heat an outer one{/idea}. With this, every basic need was covered. Adam had {reward}complete ease{/reward}, and only one tree was off limits.
now: Your marriage is good, your job is fine, your health is okay. Then one forbidden thing starts to look like the only thing that matters. {idea}One small limit can feel bigger than all the gifts.{/idea}
old: The one thing I cannot have is the thing I need most.
new: I have so much. One limit is not worth risking all of it.
try: When one forbidden thing pulls at you today, list five gifts you would risk for it.

title: Shall I show you the tree of forever?
subtitle: The whisper always offers something bigger
then: Shaytan whispered to Adam about {trap}the tree of eternity and a kingdom that never decays{/trap}. Ibn Kathir notes another verse where he {trap}swore he was a sincere well-wisher{/trap}. He kept prodding until they ate from it.
now: "This deal will set you up for life." "Just this once, it will make you happy forever." "I am only saying this because I care about you." {idea}Temptation rarely sounds like an enemy.{/idea} It sounds like a friend promising forever.
old: I would recognise a temptation easily if it came.
new: The whisper dresses up as advice and promises what it cannot give.
try: When something promises you "forever" or "everything" today, slow down and question it.

title: They ate, felt exposed, and reached for leaves.
subtitle: The first shame after the first slip
then: Adam and his wife ate, and {trap}what had been covered became exposed{/trap}. Mujahid said they {idea}patched the leaves on themselves like a garment{/idea}. Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred. The promised kingdom turned out to be shame.
now: The moment after: closing the tab, deleting the message, feeling hot in the face. {trap}The promise was pleasure; the result is wanting to hide.{/trap} That feeling is not the end. Look at the next verse.
old: After I slip, all I can do is hide and cover it up.
new: Shame after a slip is real. Adam's story shows it is not the last chapter.
try: After your next slip, do not hide it from Allah. Tell Him what you did in plain words.

title: Then his Lord chose him, forgave him, and guided him.
subtitle: The slip was not the end of Adam
then: Right after "Adam disobeyed" comes {reward}then his Lord chose him, turned to him with forgiveness, and guided him{/reward}. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith where Musa blamed Adam, and Adam answered that {idea}it had been written for him before he was created{/idea}.
now: You made a mistake that everyone in your family still brings up. You feel defined by it. {reward}Allah's last word on Adam was not the tree.{/reward} It was chosen, forgiven, guided.
old: My worst mistake is who I am.
new: Allah can choose me, forgive me and guide me after my worst slip.
try: Make sincere tawbah tonight for one mistake you feel defined by, and then let it rest.

title: Follow My guidance: no going astray, no misery.
subtitle: The promise given at the descent
then: Allah sent Adam, Hawwa and Iblis down, {trap}some of you enemies to others{/trap}. Then the promise: guidance will come. Abu Al-Aliyah said that means {idea}the Prophets, the Messengers and the evidence{/idea}. Ibn Abbas said the follower {reward}will not be misguided here or distressed in the Hereafter{/reward}.
now: Life on earth is the office politics, the traffic, the family fights. It is not Paradise. But {idea}guidance was promised for exactly this place{/idea}, and you are holding it in your hand right now.
old: Life here is just hard and I am on my own.
new: Allah sent guidance for this hard place. Following it keeps me from getting lost.
try: Pick one verse from this surah and live by it for the rest of the day.

title: Turn from My remembrance, and life gets tight.
subtitle: Comfort outside, tightness inside

row.title: outside
sub: eats, wears, lives as he likes

then: Ibn Kathir explains a life of hardship means {trap}no tranquillity and no ease in the chest{/trap}. Even if he looks comfortable, eating and wearing what he likes, {trap}his heart is in agitation and doubt{/trap}. Mujahid said being raised blind means having no proof.
now: Nice flat, good salary, holidays twice a year, and still that heavy feeling on Sunday nights. {idea}Tightness of chest is not fixed by more stuff.{/idea} Remembering Allah is what widens it.
old: If I had more money and comfort, I would feel at peace.
new: Peace lives in the chest, and it comes from remembering Allah.
try: When you feel that tightness today, stop and do two minutes of dhikr.

title: Why raise me blind, when I could see before?
subtitle: Sight that was never used
then: The one who turned from Allah's reminder will ask {trap}why have You raised me blind, when I had sight?{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains he means sight in the life of this world. Mujahid said being blind means {trap}having no proof{/trap} to offer.
now: You see everything on your phone: news, sports, every friend's holiday. Hours of looking each day. {idea}Seeing a lot is not the same as seeing what matters.{/idea} Use your eyes today for one sign of Allah.
old: I see plenty. I know what is going on in the world.
new: Real sight is noticing Allah's signs. Without that, I am looking but blind.
try: Spend five minutes today looking at something in nature and naming it as His sign.

title: You forgot Our signs, so today you are forgotten.
subtitle: The reply matches the deed
then: Ibn Kathir explains: the signs came and {trap}you dealt with them like one who does not remember them{/trap}, neglecting and ignoring them. So today you are treated like one forgotten. He notes this threat is {idea}not about forgetting memorised words while still acting on the Quran{/idea}.
now: You are trying to memorise a surah and keep losing the middle verses. That is not what this verse is about. {idea}It is about living as if the message never arrived.{/idea} Keeping its meaning alive in your day is the remedy.
old: If I forget the words I learned, I am in this verse.
new: The warning is for turning away from the signs. Living by them keeps me remembered.
try: Pick one verse you know and act on its meaning once today.

title: The Hereafter's loss is heavier and lasts longer.
subtitle: Weighing now against later
then: Allah says this is how He repays {trap}the one who transgresses and does not believe in His signs{/trap}. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter{/idea}. The warning is meant to steer choices now.
now: You hide a mistake at work to avoid embarrassment, knowing it hurts someone. Owning up costs you a bad afternoon. {idea}A hard moment here is lighter than carrying it there.{/idea}
old: Avoiding embarrassment now is worth almost anything.
new: A loss in this world is small next to what lasts. I can choose the lighter cost.
try: Own up today to one small thing you have been hiding to save face.

title: You walk through the homes of nations now gone.
subtitle: Empty houses that teach
then: Ibn Kathir explains the people of Makkah {trap}walked among the empty homes{/trap} of nations who denied their messengers. In that are signs {idea}for those with sound intellect{/idea}. He cites: it is not the eyes that grow blind, but the hearts.
now: You stroll through an old castle on holiday, take a selfie in a ruined palace. Someone once thought it would last forever. {idea}The ruins are a message, not just a backdrop.{/idea}
old: Old ruins are interesting history, nothing more.
new: Every empty palace says: what I build without Allah will not last.
try: Next time you pass an old or abandoned building, think about who once lived there.

title: Only His word and a set time hold it back.
subtitle: The delay is mercy, not absence
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah had already given His word that {reward}He would not punish anyone until the proof was established{/reward}, and at a time He set. Otherwise, {trap}the punishment would seize them immediately{/trap}.
now: You did something wrong last month and nothing happened. Life went on. It is tempting to think it did not matter. {idea}The quiet is a window to come back{/idea}, not proof that it is fine.
old: If nothing bad happened, I got away with it.
new: Allah's delay is time given to me to turn back, not a sign it does not count.
try: Use today's quiet to fix one wrong that no one has called you out on.

title: Be patient with their words, and praise through the day.
subtitle: Prayer as the answer to mockery
then: Allah comforted the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}be patient with what they say{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says before sunrise refers to Fajr and before sunset to Asr. The Prophet ﷺ, looking at a full moon, said {reward}you will see your Lord as you see this moon{/reward}, so do not miss those two prayers.
now: Someone mocks your faith in the comments, or at the family dinner. You want to fire back. {idea}Patience, then prayer{/idea}, is the answer the Prophet ﷺ was given. It ends with being pleased.
old: When people mock me, I have to win the argument.
new: I can be patient, turn to prayer, and let Allah please me with what He gives.
try: Guard Fajr and Asr today especially, and notice how they frame your day.

title: Do not stare longingly at what others enjoy.
subtitle: Their splendor is a test
then: Umar once entered on the Prophet ﷺ in a small room with almost nothing in it, and {trap}wept, thinking of Kisra and Caesar in luxury{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}those people have had their good hastened for them in this world{/idea}. Mujahid said the groups meant here are the wealthy.
now: Scrolling past a friend's new kitchen, someone's luxury holiday, the influencer's car. Your own flat suddenly feels small. {reward}What your Lord gives is better and lasts longer.{/reward} Their shine is a test for them, and staring is a test for you.
old: If they have more than me, they are better off.
new: Their splendor is short and a test. My Lord's provision is better and lasting.
try: Mute or unfollow one account today that mostly makes you envious.

title: Call your family to prayer, and keep at it yourself.
subtitle: We provide for you, not you for Us
then: Ibn Kathir notes Umar would {idea}wake his family for night prayer{/idea}, reciting this verse. Allah says He does not ask provision from you, {reward}We provide for you{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ reported Allah saying: devote yourself to My worship and {reward}I will fill your chest with richness{/reward}.
now: You skip Dhuhr because the shift is busy and you need the hours. You do not wake the kids for Fajr because they are tired. {idea}Prayer is not what makes you poor.{/idea} The One you pray to is the Provider.
old: Taking time to pray, and getting my family to pray, costs me.
new: Allah does not need my provision; He gives it. Prayer opens the door.
try: Gently invite one family member to pray one prayer with you today.

title: Why no sign? The Quran itself is the sign.
subtitle: Demanding proof while holding it
then: They asked why Muhammad ﷺ did not bring a sign. Ibn Kathir says the Quran is that proof: revealed to {idea}an unlettered man who did not study with the People of the Book{/idea}, yet it tells the past and agrees with earlier scriptures. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}what I was given is revelation{/reward}.
now: You keep waiting for a sign before you take faith seriously: a dream, a miracle, a clear answer. {idea}The sign is already on your phone, on the shelf, in the app you opened today.{/idea}
old: I need a dramatic sign before I take this seriously.
new: The greatest sign is already in my hands. I just need to read it.
try: Read the last verses of this surah again slowly, as if they were the sign you asked for.

title: No one can say: if only someone had told us.
subtitle: The messenger removes every excuse
then: Ibn Kathir explains: had Allah destroyed them before sending the Prophet ﷺ, {trap}they would have said: if only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed{/trap}. So the Messenger and the Book came, and {idea}the excuse was removed{/idea}.
now: You tell yourself, "Nobody ever taught me properly, my parents were not religious." Maybe true. But you are reading this now. {idea}It has reached you.{/idea} What you do next is yours.
old: I was never taught, so I cannot be expected to know.
new: The message has reached me now. From here, the choice is mine.
try: Learn one new thing about your faith today from a trustworthy source.

title: Everyone is waiting; you will see who walked straight.
subtitle: The surah ends with a calm challenge

row.title: it becomes clear
sub: who was on the straight path

then: Allah told the Prophet ﷺ to say to those who denied him: {idea}each of us is waiting, so wait{/idea}. You will come to know who is on {reward}the straight road{/reward} and who is guided. With this, the surah that began "not to distress you" ends without rush or anger.
now: Your relatives roll their eyes at your new habits. Your friends think you will drop them by next month. {idea}You do not have to win today.{/idea} Keep walking straight and let time show.
old: I have to prove I am right to everyone, now.
new: I can calmly keep to the straight path and let the truth reveal itself.
try: Leave one argument unfinished today, and just keep doing what is right.
